newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Foodland sees further profit rises.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Foodland sees further profit rises.

text.p: Perth-based grocery retailer and wholesaler Foodland Associated Ltd said on Thursday it expected further profit increases in Australia to come from a programme of store refurbishments, new store launches and the relaunch of its Western Australia franchises.
Foodland managing director Barry Alty said Australian net profit before abnormals rose 16.1 percent to A$38 million in the year to July 28, 1996 because of an efficiency drive.
"The two-year cost reduction and efficiency improvement programme ... will not continue to produce comparable increases in earnings," Alty said.

"Further increases in profit will come from the combination of Action's current programme of store refurbishments, new Action store openings and the relaunch of the company's Western Australian managed grocery franchises," he said.

Earlier Foodland reported a 10.1 percent fall in annual net profit to A$47.3 million and set an unchanged 16 cent final dividend. It also announced it would buy back up to 10 percent of the company's shares.
Foodland said it had been selling non-core assets over the last two years and had generated significant cash receipts.
"This cash has been used by FDL (Farmers Deka Ltd) and PEL (Progressive Enterprises Ltd ) to reduce debt," he said.

"FAL has no Australian debt and, largely because Australia does not recognise New Zealand franking credits, (Foodland) has decided against repaying the New Zealand debt raised to partially finance the acquisition of FDL and PEL," it said.

"Subject only to obtaining the prior formal consent of the majority of the creditor banks, the company has formed the view that it should enter the market to acquire a maximum of 10 percent of its shares," it said.
Foodland said it expected the buy-back to begin on October 17. Foodland owns 58 percent of Progressive.
Progressive was the main drag in Foodland's profits, with Foodland's share of Progressive's profits contributing A$1.5 million to net profits, down from from A$9.1 million in 1994/95.
"There are indications that PEL (Progressive) is capable of producing a return commensurate with FAL's holding cost," Alty said.
"There is much work to be done before PEL's full potential will be realised, but the realisation of this potential should produce future growth in earnings per share for FAL," it said.
Foodland's share price rose 15 cents to A$5.20 by 12.30 pm (0230 GMT).
